Conditional item infit MSQ

Source: R/conditional_infit.R
RMiteminfit.Rd

Computes the conditional infit mean-square (MSQ) of each item with iarm::out_infit(), and each item's location relative to the mean person location. Given the result of RMitemInfitCutoff(), it also flags misfitting items, by default on a bootstrap p-value corrected across items.

Usage

RMitemInfit(
  data,
  cutoff = NULL,
  p_value = NULL,
  correction = c("fwer", "fdr_bh", "fdr_by", "none"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  output = "kable",
  sort,
  statistic = "infit"
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Missing values (NA) are allowed, but the infit statistic uses complete cases only (see Details), so at least one is needed.

cutoff

Optional. Default NULL, no flagging. Either of:

  • The full result of RMitemInfitCutoff(). This enables the p-values (see p_value), and the caption reports the number of iterations and the interval method. A result of RMitemInfitCutoffMI() gives an error, since its simulations come from imputed data. Use it with RMitemInfitMI().

  • Its $item_cutoffs data.frame alone, with columns Item, infit_low and infit_high (or outfit_low and outfit_high with statistic = "outfit"). Items are then flagged against the interval.

Either adds the columns Infit_low, Infit_high and Flagged. Flagged gives the direction of misfit: "overfit" (below 1, or below the interval), "underfit" (above) or "" (no misfit).

p_value

Logical or NULL. Whether to flag on bootstrap p-values computed from the simulated values in cutoff. NULL (default) uses them whenever cutoff is the full RMitemInfitCutoff() result, and flags against the interval otherwise. TRUE without the full result is an error.

With FALSE, items are flagged against the interval and a one-time message gives the family-wise error rate that implies. The interval describes where a fitting item's statistic is expected to fall. Used as a decision rule over k items, a width w gives a family-wise error rate of 1 - w^k, 37% for the default 95% interval over nine items. The corrected p-value keeps the error rate at alpha and needs far fewer iterations to do so (Johansson, 2026). Versions up to 1.1.1 flagged against the interval by default, so older scripts that pass the full cutoff object may now flag different items.

correction

Character. Correction of the p-values across items when they are used: "fwer" (default, Westfall-Young step-down, controls the family-wise error rate), "fdr_bh" or "fdr_by" (Benjamini-Hochberg or Benjamini-Yekutieli, control the false discovery rate), or "none".

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1). An item is flagged when its corrected p-value is below alpha. Default 0.05. Used only with p-values.

output

Character. "kable" (default) for a knitr::kable() table, or "dataframe".

sort

Optional. sort = "infit" (or "outfit", matching statistic) sorts the rows by MSQ, largest first. Other values leave the order unchanged.

statistic

Character. Which conditional fit statistic to report and test: "infit" (default) or "outfit". Both come from the same iarm::out_infit() call and the same simulations, and the column names, interval, p-values and Flagged follow the choice. The correction is applied across the k items for the chosen statistic. Testing both statistics and reporting whichever flags is a family of 2k tests, larger than either call corrects for.

Value

  • output = "kable": a knitr_kable table with the columns "Item", "Infit MSQ" and "Relative location", and a caption with the sample size. With cutoff, also "Infit low", "Infit high" and "Flagged", and with p-values "p" and "p (adj)".

  • output = "dataframe": a data.frame with the columns Item, Infit_MSQ and Relative_location. With cutoff, also Infit_low, Infit_high and Flagged (after Infit_MSQ). With p-values, also p_infit (uncorrected two-sided p) and padj_infit (corrected p). Flagged then marks items with padj_infit < alpha, with the direction from Infit_MSQ relative to 1.

With statistic = "outfit" the columns are named after it: Outfit_MSQ, Outfit_low, Outfit_high, p_outfit, padj_outfit.

Details

Statistic. Infit MSQ is a weighted fit statistic that emphasises unexpected responses near the item's location. Values near 1 indicate fit. Values above 1 indicate underfit (responses less predictable than the model expects), and values below 1 overfit (responses more predictable). How far from 1 is too far depends on the sample size and the items, so it is judged against simulations from RMitemInfitCutoff(). No fixed value is right in general. The conditional statistic from iarm::out_infit() uses the distribution of the responses given the total score (Müller, 2020).

Data and model. The item parameters are estimated by conditional maximum likelihood with psychotools::pcmodel() (a dichotomous item is a 2-category partial credit model). The conditional infit uses complete cases only, and every response category must be used in them, or the function stops and names the item. The relative item location is the mean of the item's CML thresholds minus the mean WLE person location, a description of targeting. The iarm package must be installed (it is in Suggests).

Bootstrap p-values. Each item's observed statistic is compared with its simulated values from cutoff$results. The test statistic is the deviation from the mean of the observed and simulated values together, divided by their SD. The ZSTD (Wilson-Hilferty) transform is not used, since it does not work for the conditional MSQ (Müller, 2020). The uncorrected p is two-sided, (1 + #{|t*| >= |t|}) / (B + 1) for B simulated datasets, so it can be no smaller than 1 / (B + 1). With "fwer" the correction is the Westfall-Young step-down on the studentised maximum, which uses the dependence between the items' statistics and has more power than Bonferroni or Holm (Westfall & Young, 1993; Ferreira, 2024). Its validity rests on subset pivotality. "fdr_bh" and "fdr_by" apply Benjamini-Hochberg or Benjamini-Yekutieli. The p-values depend on the model and the sample size, and are reported with the simulated interval, not instead of it.

Iterations. The observed value is part of the mean and SD it is studentised by, so the observed and simulated statistics are exchangeable under the model, and the family-wise error rate is at the nominal level at any number of iterations in RMitemInfitCutoff(). More iterations make decisions reproducible. Two analysts using different seeds disagree about at least one item roughly 10% of the time at 400 iterations and 4% at 2000 (Johansson, 2026). A message says so below 400 iterations, and the caption below 1000. Use 1000 to 2000 for a final analysis. The uncorrected p-values are well calibrated even at a few hundred iterations.

Multiple comparisons

The uncorrected p-value controls the error rate of a single comparison. For one item (or item pair) chosen in advance it is the relevant value. Flagging whichever of k comparisons fall below alpha tests k hypotheses at once, and the chance of at least one false flag rises to about \(1 - (1 - \alpha)^k\), for example 34% for k = 8 at alpha = 0.05, even when every uncorrected p-value is calibrated. The corrected p-value controls this. correction = "fwer" bounds the probability of any false flag (strict, less power), and "fdr_bh" and "fdr_by" bound the expected share of false flags among those raised. Use the uncorrected p-value for a single comparison chosen in advance, and a corrected one when screening the whole table, which is the usual case.

Flags depend on the other items

Item infit and item-restscore both judge each item against expectations from a Rasch model fitted to all items, so misfitting items change what is expected of the others. A flag in one direction can therefore produce flags in the other. Overfitting items can push fitting items into the underfit range, and underfitting items, for example from a second dimension, can make fitting items look overfit. How large the effect is depends on how strong the misfit is and how many items share it. In simulation with seven polytomous items, two overfitting items led to about 6% of the fitting items being flagged as underfit, and one or two mildly multidimensional items to 1% to 2% being flagged as overfit. When items are flagged in both directions, consider removing the clearest misfit and testing again before interpreting the rest.

References

Ferreira, J. A. (2024). Methods of testing a 'small' or 'moderate' number of hypotheses simultaneously. Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice, 19(1), 6. doi:10.1007/s42519-024-00412-4

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

Müller, M. (2020). Item fit statistics for Rasch analysis: Can we trust them? Journal of Statistical Distributions and Applications, 7(5). doi:10.1186/s40488-020-00108-7

Westfall, P. H., & Young, S. S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing. Wiley.

See also

RMitemInfitCutoff() for the simulations, RMitemInfitPlot() to plot them with the observed values, RMitemInfitMI() for multiply imputed data, and RMitemRestscore() for a second item fit test.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("iarm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Simulate binary item response data (5 items, 40 persons)
  set.seed(42)
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(
    matrix(sample(0:1, 40 * 5, replace = TRUE), nrow = 40, ncol = 5)
  )
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:5)

  # Default kable output
  RMitemInfit(sim_data)

  # Sorted by infit MSQ descending
  RMitemInfit(sim_data, sort = "infit")

  # Return as data.frame for further processing
  df <- RMitemInfit(sim_data, output = "dataframe")

  # Simulation-based cutoffs (100 Monte-Carlo iterations)
  if (requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cutoff_res <- RMitemInfitCutoff(sim_data, iterations = 100,
                                    parallel = FALSE, seed = 42)
    RMitemInfit(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res)
    RMitemInfit(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res, output = "dataframe")

    # Bootstrap p-values with family-wise (Westfall-Young) correction
    # (use iterations >= 1000 in real analyses for stable p-values)
    RMitemInfit(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res, p_value = TRUE,
                output = "dataframe")

    # The same for conditional outfit MSQ
    RMitemInfit(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res, p_value = TRUE,
                statistic = "outfit", output = "dataframe")
  }
}
